svg.text: TTV-inspired protected gas bypass • intact airframe • structural parafoil load path • isolated battery bay
FLIGHT CONFIGURATION — BODY REMAINS ONE STRUCTURE
Rigid nonconductive cradle • two restraints • covered terminals
service joint locked for flight — does not separate

g.text: Slip fit; red tether keeps it attached.
Sleeve, ordered line stows and protector
The anchor transfers force into the body.
The servos never support the rocket.
the lines enter the protected bay.
Electronics never share the hot-gas path.
Rigid cradle, terminal cover, strain relief
No added powder and no motor modification.
Prevents the nose from becoming debris
Gas enters beneath the protector and
Carries pressure around the payload bay.
Dedicated static port serves the barometer;
it is not connected to the gas duct.

svg.text: The intact payload/body hangs below the parafoil.
Canopy → suspension risers → structural anchor → complete body
Concept derived from Apogee TTV ducted e-bay, AeroTech nose-only recovery drawings, and NPS guided-parafoil load-path research.
Not dimensioned or flight-approved. Final duct area, seals, anchor ratings, nose fit and packing sequence require CAD fit checks and supervised full-pack ground testing.
